name: Fenrir Thermal-Arc Parka
description:
A mid-length parka designed for GLMZ's brutal lake winters, manufactured by Fenrir — a Scandinavian-heritage brand that opened a Great Lakes production facility in 2171. The outer shell is a tightly woven ripstop nylon in matte black, navy, or a deep forest green. The interior uses a graphene-filament heating mesh powered by a thin flexible battery pack sewn into the left side panel — a USB-C style connector at the hem lets you charge from any standard port. Three heat settings, controlled by a simple push-button tab at the cuff. No app, no BCI sync, no cloud. Just warm.

The parka is sold in Tier 2 and Tier 3 retail channels and is considered one of the more honest pieces of heated apparel on the market — the tech is minimal, the construction is sound, and the battery lasts a full work shift at medium setting. Hood is furred with synthetic pile and detaches. Deep hand-warmer pockets. This is the parka you see on transit platforms and construction sites in January.
functionality: Integrated graphene heating mesh with three heat settings. Battery powers 8 hours on low, 4 hours on high. Charges via standard port at hem. No wireless connectivity.
what_it_says: You live in a cold city and you've made a sensible decision about it. The heated lining is a practical luxury, not a status one.
story_hooks: A batch of Fenrir parkas from a 2198 production run had a battery cell defect that causes intermittent overheating at the left side panel — not enough to catch fire, but enough to leave a burn mark on skin. Fenrir issued a quiet recall that many buyers never heard about.

The graphene mesh in the parka operates on a frequency that interferes with a specific older-model BCI handshake protocol — wearers with that implant generation sometimes experience brief signal dropout in high-cold situations. Nobody has formally connected these two facts yet.

A Shelf community organizer has been buying Fenrir parkas wholesale through a Tier 3 intermediary and distributing them to unhoused residents. Someone at Fenrir's distribution division has noticed the unusual bulk orders and flagged them.
